reality_delta: The main AI has produced an internally consistent repair narrative with clear problem descriptions and well-scoped non-goals. No implementation code exists yet for review. The delta is between the proposal narrative (which describes intent) and the code that will be written (which will contain edge-case behavior, error handling, and state-transition logic invisible at the proposal level). The three fixes share a pattern of responding to false negatives by adding fallback/relaxation paths — the cumulative effect of landing all three in one cycle is unmeasured.
main_concern: The browser interaction fix's "observable state change" criterion is undefined. Without a measurable definition (text hash, DOM mutation threshold, specific element visibility toggle), the verifier risks latching onto any incidental page side-effect — CSS transitions, XHR spinners, re-renders — inflating the pass rate without improving verification quality. The logging of all attempted candidates further creates an evidence artifact that reads as diligence but is automated fuzzing.
top_risks: Browser interaction fix inflates verification success through undefined "observable state change" criteria — verifier may accept hover effects, loading spinners, or no-op re-renders as meaningful interaction.

Signup dual-format acceptance decays the negative probe: if signups is always present as an empty array `[]`, the probe passes syntactically valid but semantically void data — violating the non-goal "不允许没有报名数据的项目通过".

Cumulative bar reduction: all three fixes relax constraints or add fallback paths in the same cycle. Without per-fix before/after evidence, the aggregate E2E strictness loss is unmeasured and violates the known constraint "Do not lower E2E strictness."
missing_evidence: Actual code diff or implementation branch for the browser interaction probe — the proposal describes intent; the implementation is where edge cases live.
Measurable definition of "observable state change" for the browser verifier — without this, the fix is a parameter without a value.
Test case showing the signup probe's behavior when signups is an empty array — needed to verify the non-goal constraint is enforced in code.
minimum_fix: Before implementation: (1) Define browser "observable state change" as a measurable criterion — minimum: page textContent hash differs pre/post interaction AND at least one non-transient DOM element was added/removed/modified. (2) Add a guard clause to the signup probe: if signups array is present but empty, the probe must fail with the same severity as missing signupIntent. (3) Consider implementing the three fixes sequentially with interleaved verification rather than landing them as a single changeset.
